title: Yama
description: Build a strong ethical foundation for your journey by exploring the five universal restraints that harmonize your relationship with the world.

sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas
sections.gurudevInsight: The husk is gone, the sprout moves though it & comes up. They are (1) Yama (2) Niyama (3) Aasana (4) Pranayama (5) Pratyahara (6) Dhyana (7) Dharana (8) Samadhi. He goes into the details of each & what is the result that you can expect from each one of them. Yoga has 8 limbs, like a chair has got four legs, yoga has 8 limbs, or legs. So you just pull 80 one, everything else will come down. If you pull one leg of the chair whole chair comes. [PDF p.80]

sutra.meaning: Ahimsa (non-violence/non-injury), Satya (truthfulness), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (right use of energy/continence), and Aparigraha (non-possessiveness/non-greed) are the five Yamas (restraints or social codes)

sections.reflectionPrompt: Did I live these today? Which can I work on? Which is difficult for me?
sections.practice: Observe yourself and note how many times you strayed or were tempted to stray from adhering to the Yamas
sections.journalPrompt: Which of the Yamas did I not follow.
sections.gurudevInsight: Ahimasa, satya, Ashteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha. Ahimsa - nonviolence Satya - Truth Astheya - non stealing Brahmacharya - moving in Brahman, moving in the bigness. jaatideshkaalsamayanva chinahsaalbhauka mahavrutta These are the greatest because it is applicable in all time in all places for all people throughout, without an interruption. There are certain laws, which can apply just to certain people, certain places, at certain time, which are not universal, but these are universal a) Ahimsa: - These 5 Principles. An animal does not go into violence for no reason. Animals hunt, even the wild animals, they hunt only when they are hungry & when they want to eat. [PDF p.81]

sutra.meaning: "These (Yamas) are the Great Vows, universal, and not limited by life-state (birth), space, time, or circumstance

sections.practice: Make a commitment to practice everywhere

sutra.meaning: There may be doubts about the claims of yoga made in this text of Sri Patanjali or made in other yoga books, however one should cast these doubts aside and practice. When the doubts arise, one should ignore the doubtful ideas and push ahead with practice.

sections.insight: The principles that prevent yama and niyama are to be countered with right knowledge and awareness.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I have doubts about the efficacy or necessity of the yamas .
sections.practice: Try to practice the yamas consciously notwithstanding the doubts you have, for today.
sections.gurudevInsight: Freedom comes with viveka or discrimination. All other species in this creation are governed by nature, totally, they don’t need discrimination nor do they have freedom. Human consciousness, human mind have this possibility of freedom, has been given freedom so it is also given discrimination. It is through this viveka, wisdom, discrimination that a human mind, human consciousness can be governed to progress or to remain where it is. You will not find any animal over eating, generally. If they are sick or perverted, they may do anything. [PDF p.80]

sections.practice: Practice kindness in word, deed and thought today
sections.journalPrompt: Did others feel calm in my presence?
sections.gurudevInsight: Someone comes to attack you, and as soon as they come near you, because your vibrations are totally nonviolent, they drop down, they stop being violent. A contemporary of Buddha is Mahavira, the promoter of Jain Religion – Jainism – his emphasis is more on Ahimsa & he said where ever he will walk, upto 20 kms around, people will all drop their violence & the story go to the extent that even the thorns will not prick anybody, the thorns would become soft & they all lie down. Established in non-violence, in your presence violence will be dropped by other creatures. Satyapratisthayaam kriyaphalashay Established in Truth, your actions will become fruitful, any act you do that will be fruitful. [PDF p.82]

Brahmacharayapratisthayam veeryalaabha d) Brahmacharya: - Said as Celibacy. Celibacy brings you strength; a lot of strength but Brahmacharya has a deeper or bigger meaning than just celibacy. Brahma means the infinity & charya means moving in the infinity. Knowing your vast nature, not thinking you are just a body but you walk like you are a glow of light, you move in the world as though you are the space. When you sitting in meditation, you don’t feel you are a body, you are a lump of a heavy weight, 80 pounds or 90 pounds or 100 pounds body, you don’t feel you are 60 kg sitting their solid. You feel so light, you feel, as though like a feather, isn’t it? [PDF p.84]

sections.insight: Stealing can be of all kinds of things- material and non material; we normally think only of the material theft.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Did I ever steal say ideas, appreciation, attention?
sections.practice: observe if you covet anything someone else has.

Anything you speak becomes a lie, the moment you open your mouth you are distorting what is & what is, is truth & to be with what is, to be truthful in ones life, ones heart is following satya, not the words. Or is their something else behind that, there are some other hooks you are keeping in, that indicates the truth, second principle - truth & the clarity in your intention, straight forwardness in your approach, the truth is the second Yama. If you look at somebody & say how nice if I had a voice like them, you have already stolen their voice. You look at someone looking beautiful Oh, how nice if I were looking like that, you have stolen. [PDF p.84]
